disclaimer: Miscanthus × giganteus is a sterile triploid hybrid of M. sinensis × M. sacchariflorus. Genomic resources are less complete than sorghum. Many entries represent well-supported projections from sorghum, maize, or Arabidopsis orthologs. Where Miscanthus-specific studies are available, they are cited directly.

evidenceLevelKey.Peer-Reviewed Literature: Gene directly characterized in Miscanthus × giganteus or M. sinensis in a published peer-reviewed study.
evidenceLevelKey.Curated Database Reference: Gene annotated in a curated plant genomics database for Miscanthus or a closely related grass.
evidenceLevelKey.Homology-Based Projection: Gene inferred from well-characterized ortholog in sorghum, maize, or Arabidopsis; functional role projected by sequence homology.
evidenceLevelKey.Environment-Relevance Estimate: Pathway relevance inferred from environmental physiology literature.

genes.name: Cinnamyl alcohol dehydrogenase
genes.functionSummary: Final step in monolignol biosynthesis — reduces cinnamaldehydes to cinnamyl alcohols. Miscanthus has lower lignin content than many grasses (approximately 10–15% by dry weight in some analyses), contributing to its high cell wall digestibility and cellulosic ethanol potential without BMR-type mutations.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus CAD; Hodgson E et al. 2010 GCB Bioenergy 2(1):23–34; sorghum SbCAD2 ortholog
genes.limitationNote: Lignin composition in Miscanthus varies by variety, tissue, and harvest date — winter harvest greatly reduces lignin penalty.

genes.name: Caffeic acid O-methyltransferase
genes.functionSummary: Methylation step in syringyl (S) lignin biosynthesis. High S:G lignin ratio in Miscanthus (often >1.0) makes it more amenable to alkaline pretreatment compared to G-dominated conifers. CoMT downregulation in Miscanthus is a target for further improving cellulosic ethanol yields.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus CoMT; Dong M et al. 2019 Bioresour Technol 284:332–339; sorghum SbCoMT (bmr12) ortholog
genes.limitationNote: Miscanthus CoMT is well-studied in the context of bioenergy cell wall improvement.

genes.name: Cellulose synthase A (multiple paralogs)
genes.functionSummary: Catalytic subunits of the rosette cellulose synthase complex. Miscanthus stems contain approximately 38–45% cellulose by dry weight — among the highest of any biomass crop. High CesA expression during rapid stem growth contributes to the exceptional biomass yield potential of Miscanthus.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus CesA; Vilela B et al. 2018 GCB Bioenergy 10(9):656–668; sorghum/maize CesA orthologs
genes.limitationNote: CesA gene family characterized in M. sinensis; M. × giganteus likely inherited high-expressing alleles from both parents.

genes.name: Pyruvate orthophosphate dikinase (C4)
genes.functionSummary: Key enzyme of C4 carbon concentrating mechanism. Miscanthus × giganteus is a C4 plant with exceptionally high light-use and nitrogen-use efficiency. Unlike most C4 grasses, Miscanthus maintains high PPDK activity at lower temperatures (down to ~8°C), contributing to its high productivity in European climates — a competitive advantage over other C4 energy crops.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus PPDK; Naidu SL et al. 2003 Plant Physiol 132(3):1688–1697; Wang D et al. 2008 Plant Physiol 148(3):1294–1301
genes.limitationNote: Cold tolerance of Miscanthus PPDK is directly studied and distinguishes M. × giganteus from other C4 crops — a defining feature.

genes.name: Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (C4 CO2 fixation)
genes.functionSummary: Primary CO2 capture enzyme in C4 photosynthesis. Miscanthus × giganteus achieves very high photosynthesis rates — among the highest recorded for any C4 grass. High PEPC activity combined with high leaf area allows Miscanthus to fix carbon at >20 Mg dry matter/ha/year under European conditions.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus PEPC; Farage PK et al. 2006 J Exp Bot 57(5):1235–1247; Long SP et al. 2006 Plant Cell Environ 29(3):351–381
genes.limitationNote: C4 photosynthesis in Miscanthus is extensively studied; PEPC kinetics at low temperature have been characterized.

genes.name: Rubisco small subunit
genes.functionSummary: Rubisco operates in bundle sheath cells in C4 plants where CO2 concentration is elevated (~1,000 ppm) by the C4 concentrating mechanism. This high CO2 suppresses photorespiration and gives C4 plants their water-use and nitrogen-use efficiency advantages over C3 crops.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus RbcS; sorghum/maize ortholog; Portis AR, Parry MAJ 2007 Photosynth Res 94(1):121–143
genes.limitationNote: Rubisco small subunit is nuclear-encoded; bundle-sheath-specific expression confirmed in C4 plants.

genes.name: C-repeat binding factor 1 (cold acclimation)
genes.functionSummary: AP2/ERF transcription factor that activates cold-responsive (COR) genes during cold acclimation. Unlike tropical C4 grasses, some Miscanthus species (M. sacchariflorus, M. sinensis) have functional cold acclimation pathways. M. × giganteus is intermediate — more cold-tolerant than sorghum but less than wheat.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus CBF; Clifton-Brown JC, Lewandowski I 2000 Ann Bot 86(2):443–452; Farrell AD et al. 2006 New Phytol 169(3):697–706
genes.limitationNote: Cold tolerance is a well-studied trait distinguishing Miscanthus from sorghum — key to its temperate climate suitability.

genes.name: Heat shock protein 70
genes.functionSummary: Major molecular chaperone of the cytoplasm and ER. HSP70 assists in folding of newly synthesized proteins and refolds heat-denatured proteins. Under summer heat stress in Texas, HSP70 induction may be critical for Miscanthus survival given its temperate-climate origin.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum SbHSP70 / Arabidopsis AtHSC70-1 ortholog; Nover L et al. 2001 Cell Stress Chaperones 6(3):177–189
genes.limitationNote: Texas heat (>38°C) is above Miscanthus optimal range — HSP induction under Texas summer heat needs direct measurement.

genes.name: Cinnamoyl-CoA reductase
genes.functionSummary: First committed step in monolignol biosynthesis — reduces cinnamoyl-CoA esters to cinnamaldehydes. CCR is a key flux-controlling step in lignin biosynthesis. Downregulation in grasses reduces lignin while increasing cellulose accessibility and cell wall digestibility.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus CCR; Barakat A et al. 2011 BMC Genomics 12:369; sorghum/maize CCR ortholog
genes.limitationNote: CCR has been characterized in Miscanthus comparative cell wall studies.

genes.name: WRKY domain transcription factor 22
genes.functionSummary: WRKY transcription factors are major regulators of both abiotic and biotic stress responses. WRKY22 class activates pathogen defense and drought stress genes. In Miscanthus, WRKY factors are implicated in coordination of cell wall lignification response to stress.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtWRKY22 (AT4G01250); Eulgem T, Somssich IE 2007 Curr Opin Plant Biol 10(4):366–371
genes.limitationNote: WRKY family is large; Miscanthus-specific WRKY characterization is limited — projection from grass orthologs.

genes.name: Dehydration responsive element-binding protein 2
genes.functionSummary: AP2-domain transcription factor activated by drought. Binds drought-responsive elements (DRE/CRT motifs) to activate protective genes. Miscanthus is moderately drought tolerant — better than sugarcane but less than sorghum or switchgrass in semi-arid conditions.
genes.orthologSource: Sorghum SbDREB2 ortholog; Arabidopsis AtDREB2A (AT5G05410); Kidokoro S et al. 2017 Plant J 92(4):679–693
genes.limitationNote: Drought tolerance in Miscanthus is less characterized than cold tolerance — a research gap given its increasing interest for drier climates.

genes.name: Sedoheptulose-1,7-bisphosphatase (Calvin cycle)
genes.functionSummary: Regulates carbon flow through the Calvin cycle in bundle sheath chloroplasts. SBPase is a major limiting step for CO2 assimilation and has been a target for photosynthesis improvement. Overexpression of SBPase in C3 plants increases photosynthesis by ~30% — an active research target in Miscanthus.
genes.orthologSource: Miscanthus SBPase; Jiang Y et al. 2016 Plant Physiol 172(4):2578–2589 (rice SBPase OE); Raines CA 2003 Photosynth Res 75(1):1–10
genes.limitationNote: SBPase as a photosynthesis bottleneck is established; Miscanthus-specific studies are emerging.

genes.name: Hydroxycinnamoyl transferase (shikimate pathway)
genes.functionSummary: Transfers hydroxycinnamic acids to shikimate in the phenylpropanoid pathway, producing the hydroxycinnamate esters used in lignin and ferulate ester biosynthesis. HCT is a major metabolic branch point. In grasses, significant amounts of p-coumarate are esterified to lignin and cell wall arabinoxylans — affecting both lignin quality and cell wall fermentability.
genes.orthologSource: Arabidopsis AtHCT (AT5G48930); Shadle G et al. 2007 Phytochemistry 68(11):1521–1529
genes.limitationNote: Hydroxycinnamic acid ester linkages in grass cell walls are critical targets for bioenergy improvement.
